indicators.note: backward tells us to read the word for students from right to left

parts.note: pupils are students at a school

explanation.surface: Slow learners in a class show that people make mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward students' reads like a jibe at weak pupils; it is the instruction to turn PUPILS round into SLIP UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip up is to make a careless mistake, the very thing that proves people are fallible.

parts.note: on a golf course, the lie is the position where the ball has come to rest
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Steering correctly: the right heading is due north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' looks like 'naturally' or a ship's course; it is a golf course, where a ball's lie is where it sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal claim to hold another person's property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: Placatory style of professional stage performer

indicators.note: a new style is a new fashioning, so the preceding word is refashioned

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A soothing, appeasing manner typical of an experienced actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A playactor is an actor in stage plays, someone paid to perform roles in a theatre.

indicators.note: moved around means the letters are shifted into another order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lead or rope is wound round a pet's neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looped around' seems to describe a lead; 'looped' is the letters and 'around' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The poodle is a curly-coated breed of canine, often clipped in elaborate styles.

indicators.note: a rider straddling a mount has it between the legs, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a girl's name
taken as written
a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

explanation.surface: A young woman of the 1600s sits astride her horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl' gives a name, the usual trick for a short run of letters; a cob is a sturdy, short-legged riding horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacobean describes the reign of James I of England, which ran through the early seventeenth century.

clue.text: People do what they like with it

definitions.text: People do what they like with it

parts.words: People do what they like with it
parts.note: surface reading: some licence or freedom that lets people behave as they please

parts.words: People do what they like with it
parts.note: setter's reading: people whose work is what they enjoy feel this contentment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Do what they like' suggests freedom from rules; read it as doing work they like.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means contentment derived from one's employment, the feeling of liking the work one does.

parts.note: surface reading: produce for timid people
setter's reading: the targets at a fairground stall where balls are thrown

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like timid; a coconut shy is a British fairground game where you throw balls to knock large hairy nuts off posts.
explanation.definitionFit: These large hard-shelled tropical palm fruits are the prizes and targets in the traditional fairground throwing game.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the thing boldness is compared to in the simile 'as bold as ...'
second meaning: an alloy of copper and zinc

explanation.surface: A fabric or substance that is rather brash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comparatively' points to a comparison: the idiom 'as bold as brass' measures boldness against this metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The familiar simile compares a shameless person with this metal, which is also a yellow alloy of copper and zinc.

clue.text: It's put in by an attendant or 3 down in 21 down

definitions.text: It's put in by an attendant
definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who attends 'puts in' this, by turning up
second meaning: what a stage performer makes in a play

explanation.walkthrough: 'Attendant' looks like a servant or usher; it means someone who attends. 3 down and 21 down are PLAYACTOR and DRAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: To put in an appearance is to show up, and an actor's role in a play is also called an appearance.

clue.text: High explosive combat may produce many victims

parts.note: HE is the standard abbreviation for high explosive

indicators.note: what a word may produce is something made from its letters, a fresh arrangement of them

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Explosives used in battle can cause a great many casualties.
explanation.definitionFit: A hecatomb was originally a sacrifice of a hundred oxen, and now means any great slaughter of people or animals.

clue.text: Many lights used in the theatre

definitions.text: Many lights used in the theatre

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
lamps are lights

explanation.surface: A stage is lit by a great many lamps.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: theatre lanterns are hung from the rigging bars by clamps, so clamps hold many of the lights used in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage lighting units are fixed to overhead bars with metal clamps, so many stage lights rely on them.

clue.text: Festival in various lands — Italy's a possibility

indicators.note: various suggests differing forms, so the letters take a different order
one possibility among many arrangements of the letters is the one wanted

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged, with the A that follows
taken as written, part of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A feast kept in several countries, perhaps including Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true: All Saints' Day, 1 November, is a public holiday in Italy and many other countries.
explanation.definitionFit: All Saints' Day is a Christian feast honouring every saint, held each year on the first of November.

clue.text: Where one may find a small jumper with a big top?

definitions.text: Where one may find a small jumper with a big top?

parts.words: a small jumper with a big top
parts.note: surface reading: a little knitted pullover with an oversized collar or neck

parts.words: a small jumper with a big top
parts.note: setter's reading: a tiny leaping insect performing in a show held under a tent

explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater; the big top is the circus tent, and the small jumper is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a novelty show in which trained insects supposedly perform tricks, a miniature version of the travelling tented show.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dull, lacking liveliness; in music, a note lowered in pitch
second meaning: a set of rooms on one floor to live in

explanation.surface: A modest, unshowy little home.
explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a modest house; split, one half is dull or musically lowered and the other is a home. A flat is the British word for an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flat is lifeless and subdued, and a flat is the British term for an apartment on one level.

definitions.note: read as 'belonging to the whole', an adjectival sense

indicators.note: possibly means the following word could be arranged another way

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that may concern the entirety of a thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relating to the whole' looks like one phrase defining the answer; 'relating' is in fact the anagram material, leaving 'to the whole' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral describes a part that belongs to and is essential for completing an entire thing.

parts.note: good means proper or correct
looks means searches

explanation.surface: Justice requires thorough, correct investigations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairness' looks like justice; here it means beauty, as in a fair face.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairness in the old sense means beauty, and good looks are an attractive appearance.

indicators.note: one thing concealing another hides it within itself

parts.note: fees are charges for a service
ores are minerals mined for metal

explanation.surface: Someone expects to be charged for hiding mining deposits.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to predict or expect something before it happens, which is to anticipate it.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to bring something off well

definitions.note: noun phrase for a verb; the question mark allows it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to take someone away by force

explanation.surface: A kidnapper wonders whether the snatch was pulled off well.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry off a task is to accomplish it, and to carry off a person is to seize and take them away.

clue.text: A small number back church no longer

indicators.note: back says the abbreviation is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number, a small form of the word
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Only a few people still go to church, unlike before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A small number' is the shortened word No., not a low figure like one or two.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some time in the past but not now.

clue.text: Sounds like conversation has a twist

indicators.note: sounds like says it is the pronunciation of the next word that matters

parts.note: talk is conversation; in a British accent without a sounded r the two words are pronounced the same

explanation.surface: A chat that contains an unexpected turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A twist' seems to be a plot twist in the talk; it is the definition, a twisting force.
explanation.definitionFit: Torque is a rotational force, the turning effect that makes something rotate around an axis.

parts.note: surface reading: any institution of learning
setter's reading: a place of education that sits in the centre, between primary and secondary levels

explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre' seems to mean a building; it means the middle of the age range, a school between junior and senior stages.
explanation.definitionFit: This type of school takes children between primary and senior stages, the midpoint of their schooling.

clue.text: Large number in new RADA production

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other
new suggests a fresh version, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A big cast appears in a fresh show by the London acting academy.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange RADA to DRAA and put M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play or stage production, something put on for an audience.

parts.note: taken as written
re means about, concerning; on shows it follows

explanation.surface: A man keeps going on about being at the event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going on about' suggests nagging, but 'on' just means placed after, and 'about' is RE, from the Latin 'in re', as in business letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Here means in this place, at hand, which is to be present.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a meagre smear on bread
second meaning: an awkward fix or predicament

explanation.surface: A slice of bread with a little butter and some fruit preserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam' looks like the preserve on the toast; it is a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape of butter is a thin smear of it, and a scrape is also a tight spot or difficulty.

clue.text: Sort of question found in inverted commas

definitions.text: Sort of question found in inverted commas

parts.note: surface reading: a kind of query, as if a category of question is wanted
setter's reading: the position of a quoted remark, a question placed within quotation marks

explanation.walkthrough: Inverted commas is the British name for quotation marks; the clue describes where a quoted question sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Words placed within quotation marks are said to be enclosed that way, which is what inverted commas are.

clue.text: He killed a couple of fools in the end

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a noun: one who killed

parts.note: an ass is a fool, and a couple means two of them
the word in, placed at the end

explanation.surface: A murderer ultimately did away with two idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the end' reads as 'finally'; it tells you to put IN at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, specifically one who kills a prominent person by surprise attack.

clue.text: Proceeded to take legal action in the finish

indicators.note: in places one phrase inside the other

parts.note: the end is the finish
to sue is to take someone to court

explanation.surface: Someone went on to bring a lawsuit at the last moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensued means followed on or happened next, as a sequel to something earlier.
